senses.def: a state of intensive joy and gladness, often implying verbal expression and body movement (for example, jumping, leaping, dancing)

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: pertaining to being without a special goal or purpose
senses.comment: In a number of languages ‘aimlessly’ may be rendered simply as ‘without having some goal’ or ‘without some reason’ or ‘without trying to accomplish something.’

senses.def: pertaining to being shamefully greedy for material gain or profit
pertaining to not being able to speak or talk
(derivative of μεταμέλομαι[a] ‘to regret,’ 25.270, with a negative prefix) pertaining to not feeling regret as the result of what one has done

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to not being guilty of wrongdoing
to move away from a location, implying a considerable distance
to move back to a point or area from which one has previously departed, but with more explicit emphasis upon the return (compare ὑποστρέφω[a], 15.88)
to pay something back to someone as the result of an incurred obligation
to cause someone to suffer in turn because of actions which merit such retribution
pertaining to being not prepared
to change to a previous good state
senses.comment: A rendering of ἀποκαθίστημι in Mark 3:5 as was healed is justified on the basis that at a previous time the hand was crippled, but ἀποκαθίστημι in and of itself does not mean to be healed. Note, however, a contrasting situation in ἰάομαι[b] (13.66).

senses.def: to send someone back to a place where one has been before
the state of being absent
(derivative of ἁρπάζω[a] ‘to carry off by force,’ 57.235) one who carries off the possessions of another by force
senses.comment: For an interpretation of ἅρπαξ as an adjective in Luke 18:11, see 25.25.

senses.def: pertaining to being destructively vicious
pertaining to being violently greedy
senses.comment: In Luke 18:11 ἅρπαξ may also be interpreted as a noun (see 57.239).

senses.def: pertaining to being beautiful or attractive in terms of being well-formed
(derivative of ἀφανίζομαι[a] ‘to become invisible,’ 24.27) pertaining to that which becomes invisible
(an idiom, literally: to hear heavily with the ears) to be mentally slow or dull in comprehending
(derivative of βιάζομαι[b] ‘to use violence,’ 20.10) a person who employs violence in order to accomplish his purpose
senses.comment: See the comment at 20.10 for a discussion of some of the problems involved in the interpretation of this type of expression.

senses.def: the relatively deep area of the sea or ocean sufficiently far from land as to be beyond the range of any protection from the seacoast
senses.comment: In order to designate the high sea or the ocean, it may be necessary in some instances to speak of ‘the sea far from land’ or ‘the sea out of sight of land.’ People who live near the ocean and are seafaring frequently have quite distinct terms for different conditions of the sea, whether, for example, it is stormy, moderately rough, or relatively calm. Languages may also use different terms in speaking of different areas of the sea or ocean. Note, for example, in English the use of China Sea, North Sea, Bering Sea, in contrast with Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean. In English this contrast is relatively fixed, but it does reflect a gradation of size, since sea is used normally in speaking of smaller areas than is the case with ocean.

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: to become old in age (referring to living beings)
(derivative of δανείζω ‘to lend money,’ 57.209) a person whose business it is to lend money to others at an interest rate
to make an obscurity clear by a thorough explanation
to inform in detail and with clarity
one who presides over a court session and pronounces judgment
the course that one follows in a race
senses.comment: The context of 2 Timothy 4:7 is figurative.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of δρόμος[a] ‘race,’ 50.5) a task or function involving continuity, serious effort, and possibly obligation

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (derivative of ἐγκρατεύομαι ‘to exercise self-control,’ 88.83) pertaining to exercising self-control
to move out of an enclosed or welldefined two or three-dimensional area
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἐκπνέω ‘to breathe out,’ not occurring in the NT) to engage in the final act of dying
(derivative of ἕλκος ‘sore, ulcer,’ 23.179) to have sores on the body
cardinal number, where there are eleven instances of a countable entity
senses.comment: Οἱ ἕνδεκα: With the article, refers to the eleven disciples after Judas left

senses.def: to experience dreams having the significance of visions
senses.comment: For a discussion of some of the problems involved in terms for ‘dream,’ see 33.486.

senses.def: (derivative of ἐπαγγέλλομαι[a] ‘to promise,’ 33.286) the content of what is promised
the content of one’s agreement or approval
senses.comment: In ἐπαγγελία[b] the focus is upon the communication of agreement or approval. One may, therefore, translate 'and are waiting for your approval´ in Acts 23:21 as 'and are waiting for a message from you concerning your agreement´ or 'and are waiting for word from you as to your approval.´

senses.def: to write on a surface
(a technical and medical term) to pull the foreskin over the end of the penis as a means of concealing former circumcision
senses.comment: A literal and descriptive rendering of ἐπισπάομαι could prove to be quite vulgar in some languages. Furthermore, such a practice might seem to be medically impossible or absurd, so that in general, translators have used some such expression as ‘do not conceal the circumcision’ or ‘do not change the circumcision to appear like uncircumcision,’ but often some additional marginal note is required if people are to understand satisfactorily what is involved.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: a feeling of resentfulness based upon jealousy and implying rivalry
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐριθεία in Philippians 1:17, see 39.7.|The meaning of ‘rivalry’ may be expressed as ‘wanting to be better than someone else’ or ‘wanting to make people think they are better.’ The meaning of ‘selfish ambition’ may be rendered as ‘what they do is just to make themselves look bigger’ or ‘what they do is just for themselves.’

senses.def: a feeling of hostility or opposition
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐριθεία in Philippians 1:17 as meaning ‘selfish ambition’ or ‘rivalry’ (see 88.167).

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: a favorable occasion for some event

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: pertaining to recurring on a daily basis

senses.subdomain: Speaker and Those Associated with the Speaker [exclusive and inclusive]
senses.def: pertaining to the speaker or writer and those associated with him or her, either including or excluding the audience
senses.comment: This meaning is also found as a variant reading: κατὰ τὸν ἡμέτερον νόμον ἐβουλήθημεν ἀνελεῖν ‘we wished to judge him according to our law’ Acts 24:6 (apparatus).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to hatred for God
senses.comment: It is possible, though unlikely, that θεοστυγής in Romans 1:30 could be interpreted as ‘those whom God hates.’

senses.def: one of the twelve apostles; see also 93.95
(derivative of Ἰουδαῖος ‘a Jew,’ 93.172) pertaining to the Jewish nation
to seize and fasten onto
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to translate this expression in Acts 28:3 as ‘a snake bit his hand and did not let go.’

senses.def: a construction used for the smelting of ore and burning of ceramic ware
senses.comment: In Matthew 13:42 and Matthew 13:50 κάμινος is used figuratively of hell.|In rendering the meaning of κάμινος, the emphasis should be upon the extreme heat, rather than upon the particular type of construction.

senses.def: to judge someone as definitely guilty and thus subject to punishment
glosses: to render a verdict of guilt

senses.def: to mutilate by severe cutting (occurring in Philippians 3:2 as an exaggerated reference to περιτομή ‘circumcision,’ 53.51)
senses.comment: It is possible that κατατομή in Philippians 3:2 means ‘those who practice mutilation’ (as a hyperbole for circumcision) in the same way that περιτομή in some contexts means ‘those who circumcise.’

senses.def: a Roman officer in command of about one hundred men
senses.comment: In a number of languages, centurion can very readily be rendered by a phrase such as ‘a commander of a hundred soldiers,’ but in many instances the closest natural equivalent is simply ‘captain.’

senses.def: pertaining to having been called
senses.comment: As in the case of the translation of meanings in 33.312 and 33.313, it may be necessary likewise to make certain semantic adjustments in the translation of κλητός[a]. For example, the phrase in Romans 1:1 may be rendered as ‘urgently invited to be an apostle’ or even ‘summoned and commissioned to be an apostle.’

senses.def: pertaining to having been invited
senses.comment: It is possible that this expression in Matthew 22:14 was a common popular saying, namely, an adage. There are certain problems in the understanding of this adage in Matthew 22:14, for it would seem as though many persons are invited to do something, but few are permitted to do it. Perhaps this should be understood in the sense of ‘many are invited to apply, but few are selected.’ In this context, of course, both the invitation and the selection would be by God.

senses.def: a Hebrew dry measure for grain, flour, etc., of between ten and twelve bushels or about 390 liters
the motion of an object rolling back and forth or rolling about
senses.comment: It is rare that one can use in a language the same or related terms for the rolling of a person in an epileptic fit and the wallowing of a pig in the mud. The first is chaotic and uncontrolled, while the second is both purposeful and slower.

senses.def: (derivative of λειτουργέω[a] ‘to serve,’ 35.22) pertaining to service

wild, four-footed, predatory canine; light-brown fur, similar to jackal, but much bigger; Canis lupus; regarded as ravenous and fierce; commonly prey on flocks; symbol of roaming, opportunistic, dangerous, fierce, and clever banditry
senses.comment: In areas of the world in which wolves are not known, some translators have rendered λύκος[a] by the local equivalent of ‘leopard’ or ‘jaguar.’ This may be satisfactory for initial translations of the Scriptures, but such shifts in reference are normally rejected at a later stage by those readers who become more acquainted with the types animals which exist in other parts of the world. In most instances in which local terms for ‘wolf’ do not exist, translators have used descriptive phrases such as ‘wild dog’ or ‘fierce, wild dog,’ or they may have borrowed a term from a dominant language in the area and have added a qualifying phrase, for example, ‘a wild animal called wolf.’ One may, of course, simply use a more generic expression with some kind of qualifier. For example, in Acts 20:29 it is possible to use ‘fierce, wild animals,’ for the meaning of the passage is primarily figurative, and a specific designation of wolf is not required.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of λύκος[a] ‘wolf,’ 4.11) a person who is particularly vicious and dangerous
senses.comment: In situations where wolves are not known, it may be possible to translate Acts 20:29 as ‘men like fierce animals will come among you.’ In some instances λύκος in Acts 20:29 has been rendered as ‘fierce, wild dogs.’

senses.def: the miraculous food given by God to the Israelites during their journey through the wilderness
senses.comment: In most languages μάννα is rendered by a transliteration as ‘manna’ or ‘mana.’ One must, however, be very careful about the transliteration of this term, since it may correspond to an indigenous expression having quite a different meaning. Although in the OT it may be useful to have a marginal note explaining the play on words involved in the derivation of this term, in the NT one can usually use an expression such as ‘food called manna.’

senses.def: a relatively emphatic marker of contrast

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
senses.def: the negation of extending time up to and beyond an expected point
the nature or character of something, with emphasis upon both the internal and external form
senses.comment: In view of the lack of a closely corresponding lexical item such as ‘nature,’ it may be necessary to restructure the form of Philippians 2:7 as ‘he became truly a servant.’

senses.subdomain: Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
senses.def: a visual form of something

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of νέφος ‘cloud,’ not occurring in the NT) a large crowd of people
senses.comment: In Hebrews 12:1 a possible supplementary component of ‘heavenly’ is applicable, since the reference is to the heroes of faith mentioned in chapter 11. In general one cannot preserve the figure of speech, nor even a term meaning ‘crowd,’ since the persons in chapter 11 did not form a crowd historically. A more common equivalent of ‘large crowd of witnesses’ is ‘many, many witnesses.’

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: a period consisting of a night and a day (essentially similar in meaning to ἡμέρα[a] ‘day,’ 67.178, but somewhat more explicit and emphatic)

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to shrinking from or hesitating to engage in something worthwhile, possibly implying lack of ambition
pertaining to being bothersome
glosses: to be a bother to not mind (in combination with οὐκ)

senses.def: interrogative references to class or kind

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: an indefinite negated point of time
one who manages an inn as a place where people may obtain board and room at a price
senses.comment: In some languages it may be necessary to describe the role of an inn or hotel as ‘a place where people could stay overnight and get something to eat’ or even ‘a place where people could pay in order to stay overnight and get something to eat.’

senses.def: to sail to and beyond a particular point
to suffer pain
to undergo an experience, usually difficult, and normally with the implication of physical or psychological suffering
senses.comment: The first statement in Galatians 3:4 is generally interpreted as referring to the valuable experiences which the Galatians had in receiving the Spirit on the basis of hearing and believing. Some scholars, however, understand πάσχω in Galatians 3:4 as referring to difficult experiences resulting from those who opposed this new faith in Jesus Christ.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to meddle in the affairs of someone else
senses.comment: In some languages one may speak of a busybody as ‘one who puts his spoon in someone else’s cup’ or ‘one who always tells another how to buy and sell.’

senses.def: traditionally the distance from the elbow to the end of the fingers, about eighteen inches or one-half meter
senses.comment: The interpretation of πῆχυς in Matthew 6:27 as a measurement of stature rather than length of life may be justified as an instance of literary hyperbole or exaggeration. Most modern translations, however, interpret πῆχυς in this context as a reference to length of life rather than as a measurement of height (see discussion under ἡλικία[a] in 67.151).

senses.def: an abundance of possessions exceeding the norm of a particular society and often with a negative connotation
senses.comment: ‘Your riches’ in James 5:2 may be expressed by means of a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘all the many things you possess.’

senses.def: a high point on any scale and having the implication of value as well as abundance
senses.comment: In a number of languages, the expression τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ in Ephesians 1:7 would need to be translated as ‘he is very, very kind.’ Though syntactically ὁ πλοῦτος is the nominal head of the phrase in Ephesians 1:18, semantically ὁ πλοῦτος indicates the extent of the δόξα, and δόξα, in turn, clarifies the nature of the κληρονομία.

senses.def: interrogative of quantity of objects or events, usually implying a considerable amount
interrogative of quantity
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be necessary in Luke 16:5 to employ an expression relating to countable objects, for example, ‘how many pieces of money do you owe my master?’ (see 59.5).

senses.def: a relatively high point on a scale involving exclamation
senses.comment: In a number of languages an expression of high degree in an exclamation can only be reproduced as an expression of intensive degree in a non-exclamatory form. For example, the statement in Matthew 6:23 ‘how great must the darkness be!’ must be rendered in a number of languages as ‘the darkness is very, very intense’ or ‘it is very, very dark there.’

senses.def: to spread good news in advance of its happening (in the NT, restricted in reference to the good news about Jesus Christ)
glosses: to bring the good news ahead of time

senses.def: to call to, with a possible implication of a reciprocal relation
to urgently invite someone to accept responsibilities for a particular task, implying a new relationship to the one who does the calling
senses.comment: It is rare that one can translate καλέω[d], κλῆσις[a], and προσκαλέω[b] as simply ‘to call’ in the sense of ‘to speak to someone at a distance and tell them to come.’ For example, in 2 Thessalonians 2:14 it may be necessary to render the above clause as ‘through the good news we preached, which summoned you to do this.’ Similarly, in Acts 16:10 one may translate ‘because God has urgently invited us to preach the good news to the people there.’

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: the early part of the daylight period
a person in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:4; Luke 3:32, apparatus)

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the fleshy part on either side of the face
senses.comment: Though in many languages there is a specific term for ‘cheek,’ in some instances it may be necessary to use a phrase meaning ‘the side of the head’ or ‘the side of the face.’

senses.def: to cause trouble or harassment
to suffer trouble or harassment
senses.comment: In Luke 7:6 σκύλλου can perhaps be best rendered in some languages by supplying a pronoun, for example, ‘do not bother yourself’ or ‘do not trouble yourself’ or even ‘do not cause yourself difficulty.’

senses.def: to groan or sigh as the result of deep concern or stress
senses.comment: To groan or to sigh may be the result of quite different circumstances, and in a number of languages a clear distinction must be made in any term for groaning or sighing, depending upon the reason or basis for such an expression of emotion. In Mark 7:34 the sigh or groan would seem to be an expression of sympathy for the deaf-mute, but in Mark 7:34 the groans would be caused by severe misery and oppression.

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of στενάζω[a] ‘to groan, to sigh,’ 25.143) to complain in an intensive and excessive manner
senses.comment: It may even be possible to retain something of the figurative meaning of στενάζω in James 5:9 by translating ‘do not complain with moaning’ or ‘do not moan and complain against.’

senses.def: to catch in a net (animals or fish)
(a figurative extension of meaning of συγκλείω ‘to enclose,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause to happen, with the implication of significant restrictions
to give assent to a particular proposition
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to give assent to’ is simply ‘to say Yes to.’ In other instances it may be important to introduce direct discourse, for example, ‘to say, I agree.’

senses.def: to break or shatter a solid object into pieces, with the implication of destruction

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: to engage actively and earnestly in some activity over a period of time
to be empty, with special reference to a dwelling
a degree of completeness, with the possible implication of purpose or result
one who is particularly bold and daring
pertaining to being unable to see
(a figurative extension of meaning of τυφλός[a] ‘unable to see, blind,’ 24.38) pertaining to not being able to understand
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is possible to preserve the figurative meaning of ‘blind’; in certain instances, however, part of the figurative meaning may be retained by translating ‘not able to see how to live’ or ‘not able to see the truth.’

senses.subdomain: Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
senses.def: to regard a person as being exceptionally honored in view of high status
a location above the earth and associated with supernatural events or beings
senses.comment: There are differences of scholarly opinion as to whether ὕψωμα in Romans 8:39 is to be understood as a dimension of space (and as such, related to certain Pythagorean or NeoPlatonic concepts of elemental forces) or as the world above (as the location of alien demonic forces). For another interpretation of ὕψωμα in Romans 8:39, see 12.46.|In contexts in which these expressions refer clearly to ‘heaven’ or ‘the sky,’ it is better to use terms meaning ‘heaven’ or ‘sky’ rather than terms meaning ‘height’ or ‘that which is high.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ὕψωμα[a] ‘world above,’ 1.13) supernatural powers in the region above the earth
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ὕψωμα in Romans 8:39, see 1.13.|It is possible that ὕψωμα in Romans 8:39 should be interpreted merely as a reference to the distance which a person might be separated from God.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ὕψωμα ‘height,’ not occurring in the NT) an exaggerated evaluation of what one is or of what one has done
a person greeted in Romans 16:15
a three-dimensional object with irregular rounding contours
(derivative of φυράω ‘to mix substances’ such as flour, either with other dry substances or with water, not occurring in the NT) that which is mixed or kneaded

senses.comment: In the NT χιών occurs only as a symbol of complete whiteness, and hence in those cases in which a receptor language may not have any term for snow, it is possible to use a nonfigurative expression such as ‘very, very white.’ In a number of languages, however, there may not be a specific term for snow but a type of descriptive phrase reflecting people’s knowledge about snow, even though the substance may not occur in their immediate vicinity. For example, in some instances snow is spoken of as ‘volcano frost.’ In certain parts of the world, however, the translator’s problem is not in finding a term for snow but in distinguishing between a number of different terms which designate distinct types of snow and snow formations. Under such circumstances one can simply use for ‘snow’ an expression which suggests the whitest variety or that form of snow which is most commonly referred to.

senses.def: (derivative of ψευδομαρτυρέω ‘to testify falsely,’ 33.271) the content of what is testified falsely
